options.why: Multiplied by $43$ instead of $0.43$, treating the percentage as a whole number.

questions.question_text: Alex needs $45\%$ of an $80$ mL bottle of syrup. Bo needs $4.5\%$ of an $800$ mL bottle of syrup. Who needs more syrup?

options.text: They need the same amount; both need $36$ mL.
Bo, because $800$ mL is ten times as much syrup.
options.why: Compared only the bottle sizes, ignoring that Bo's percentage is ten times smaller.

options.text: Alex, because $45\%$ is ten times the percentage Bo uses.
options.why: Compared only the percentages, ignoring that Bo's bottle is ten times larger.

questions.solution_text:
$45\%\times80=0.45\times80=36$
$4.5\%\times800=0.045\times800=36$
They need the same amount, $36$ mL each.
